objective: Deliver NewFang's first daily-use workflow: source request or planning document -> repository orientation -> structured intake draft -> understanding check -> accepted project truth -> next justified action -> durable resume.

findings.statement: A source request or planning document must flow through orientation, structured intake, understanding check, acceptance, next action, and durable resume.
The language model performs interpretation; NewFang owns preservation, schemas, lifecycle, review, application, persistence, provenance, and resumability.
Model-generated interpretations are never applied to canonical project truth silently; the user reviews an understanding check first.
Schema version 3 is introduced with an explicit 2 -> 3 migration (inspect, --apply, backup, atomic replace).
Locked decisions, proposals, examples, assumptions, and open questions must remain distinguishable, and source terminology is preserved rather than silently corrected.
Repository orientation uses repository-local information only unless the user explicitly requests research, and orientation artifacts exclude secrets and absolute private paths.
Intake sources are preserved byte-for-byte with a verified SHA-256, rejecting absolute paths, traversal, and symlink escapes.
Applying the same reviewed revision twice creates nothing new, and exact duplicates of existing decisions, risks, and work items are not recreated.
Restart restores intake, brief, orientation, focus, and next action.

Claims, runtime verification receipts, protected completion, delegation, approval bundles, background processes, sandboxing, remote execution, model-routing policy, cost tracking, and release automation are out of scope for this phase.
Interpretation of planning documents is nondeterministic, so the understanding check and human acceptance are the only guarantees that canonical truth is correct.
findings.note: Inferred from the interpretation-vs-enforcement split; the source does not state this as a risk.

findings.statement: How should a revision request from the user be captured — as a new draft revision only, or also as a durable record of what was corrected?
Repository-local orientation is sufficient for this phase; no external research is required.

proposedWorkItems.title: Capture intake revision requests as durable review records
proposedWorkItems.description: Today a revision request produces a new draft revision but no durable record of what the user asked to change. Decide whether to record review feedback alongside the draft.
acceptanceCriteria: a revision request is recorded or explicitly documented as out of scope

proposedNextAction: Build claims, verification receipts, and the protected completion transition (NF-3).
proposedNextActionRationale: Intake, orientation, and the Steward context loop now work end to end, so the next unproven promise is evidence-before-completion: NF-1 has been implemented and tested for two packets but still cannot be marked complete because no protected completion transition exists. NF-3 closes that gap and unblocks NF-4 and the self-hosting gate.
reviewNotes: Existing accepted decisions (DEC-1..DEC-6), risks (RSK-1..RSK-4), and roadmap items (NF-1..NF-7) were deliberately not re-proposed; only genuinely new Phase 3 findings are included.
